title: Surge lanes & scope-hedge framework for capacity-constrained cycles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Upcoming product cycles show tight engineering headcount against high-priority roadmap items (Optimizer, Dedicated autoscaling, Console rollout). We need a repeatable approach to reserve staffing 'surge lanes', define scope-hedging (graceful cuts) and create a decision playbook that PMs/EMs can use at the start and mid-cycle to keep commitments while minimizing regression risk.

Proposed outcome: Deliver a lightweight template and operational runbook that contains 1) a swimlane model for pre-allocated surge capacity (per discipline), 2) a scope-cut matrix tied to OKRs and customer impact, 3) a roster & escalation process for surge staffing, 4) a fast re-prioritization checklist for mid-cycle adjustments, and 5) one pilot cycle implementation and retro.

Key decisions to make: how many FTE-hours to reserve per cycle tier (Small/Medium/Large), whether surge lanes are pooled or per-project, whether we allow fractional cross-team borrow, and what automated signals (velocity, SLA alerts) trigger surge activation.

Success metrics: reduced number of mid-cycle scope rollbacks by 40%, average cycle on-time delivery of P1 features increase by 20%, response time from request to surge activation <48h, and clear reduction in urgent post-release incidents attributable to rushed scope cuts.

Artifacts: Confluence playbook draft (link below), Google Sheet for capacity model, sample scope-cut matrix and OKR-mapping template.
